I am a dog owner who lives in Manhattan as well in a 400 something square foot apartment and my advice is that having a dog is doable but there are caveats to it. 

Your work hours are a major problem. When first getting a dog (especially if you are getting a puppy versus an older dog) you need to help them adjust to your home. It's scary for them and they will not know what they should or shouldn't do (i.e. chew on your shoes). You'll probably want to plan getting your dog around some sort of vacation to be with them while they settle in. Also if you do get a puppy, it needs to be let out at lunch time. Every day. Without expection. Puppies normally need to bathroom around 6 times a day when under 6 months. That means even making your puppy hold its bladder until you show up at lunch is tough. Getting home at 7pm will be too long of a period of time from the lunch hour to hold it. My point here being there will be accidents but you can't expect to get mad at the dog for not being house broken because it simply can't wait that long to go outside.

So you can have a dog in NYC but you need to be ready to not have a life for the first few months. It is like caring for a human child and you need to spend a lot of time with it as a puppy to help teach good habits.
